abstention.note: A false assertion is the system answering a question it cannot answer. For a tool that proposes candidate identities this is the failure that produces a wrong name, so it is reported separately from recall rather than averaged into it. Thresholded and unthresholded runs are both reported: the difference is the finding, and publishing only the better number would hide that a threshold is doing the work.

limitations: Attribution results are SYNTHETIC PERSONA RETRIEVAL, not validated human authorship attribution. Personas are generated with known parameters, so recovering them recovers the generator.
Sample size is small: 12 clustered services across 4 clusters, 20 personas. Confidence intervals are reported because the point estimates alone would overstate what the sample supports.

Thresholds are fitted on dev and frozen before any test score exists, but the module tables score the whole farm; only the `held_out` block is scored entirely on unseen operators (2 of 4 clusters, 6 services). A held-out figure from a sample that small carries a wide interval, and M3 and M5 are not split that way at all -- their truth is persona- and pair-based -- so their headline numbers include clusters the thresholds were fitted on.

Frequency filtering addresses widespread vendor-default artefacts and not coincidental ones. The coincidental class needs a maintained blocklist of known defaults, which this implementation does not have.

Every rule has an implemented hard-negative fixture: the false-positive rate is measured against a fixture that trips the rule's pattern without its meaning, so no rule is scored only against true positives.
Provenance establishes byte consistency against a recorded digest. It is not chain of custody and does not establish admissibility.
